A.explanation: Too small. $0.20\text{ N s}$ would need only a $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ velocity change for a $0.10\text{ kg}$ mass.

B.explanation: This subtracts speeds as $0.10 \times (20-15)$. It ignores that momentum is a vector and the $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ rebound is in the opposite direction.

C.explanation: This is only the magnitude of the final momentum, $0.10 \times 15$. Change in momentum needs final minus initial with signs.

D.explanation: With opposite directions, the total velocity change is $20+15=35\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $\Delta p = 0.10 \times 35 = 3.5\text{ N s}$.

hints: Notice the $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ approach and $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$ rebound are in opposite horizontal directions, so give them opposite signs.
Recall change in momentum is $\Delta p = m v - m u$, not $m$ times the difference of the speeds.
Add the two speed magnitudes because reversing direction increases the total change, then multiply by $0.10\text{ kg}$ to get $\text{N s}$.
walkthrough: Choose a positive direction, for example towards the bat. Then $u = +20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and the rebound velocity is $v = -15\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the rule for change in momentum: $\Delta p = mv - mu = m(v-u)$.
The magnitude of the change is $3.5\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, which is $3.5\text{ N s}$ since $1\text{ N s} = 1\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
